record.question:
A company has two interconnected data centers. Applications in an AWS VPC depend on systems reachable through either data center. A single Site-to-Site VPN connection currently terminates on one customer gateway device in the first data center and uses a virtual private gateway attached to the VPC. Both VPN tunnels are configured.

Which change removes the customer gateway device and first data center as single points of connectivity failure?

options.text: Deploy a separate customer gateway device with an independent internet connection in the second data center. Create another Site-to-Site VPN connection to the existing virtual private gateway and configure routing through both connections.
Deploy a NAT gateway in the second data center and use it as the termination point for an additional AWS VPN tunnel.
Create another virtual private gateway in a second Availability Zone and attach it to the same VPC while retaining the existing customer gateway device.
Create a second virtual private gateway, attach it concurrently to the same VPC, and connect a second customer gateway device to it.

explanation.text:
<<1>> adds an independent on-premises failure domain while reusing the managed virtual private gateway. Each VPN connection has two tunnels, and routing must advertise the necessary prefixes through both customer gateways. The data-center network must also maintain access to the dependencies through the surviving location.

<<2>> treats a NAT gateway as a VPN customer gateway device; these are different functions, and an AWS NAT gateway is a VPC resource. <<3>> retains the failing on-premises device and incorrectly treats a virtual private gateway as a customer-selected zonal resource. <<4>> assumes that two virtual private gateways can be attached concurrently to one VPC.

Two tunnels protect against AWS-side tunnel endpoint failures, but both can fail together if they share one customer gateway device, internet connection or data center.

AWS documentation (checked 2026-09-18):
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/vpn-redundant-connection.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/vpn-limits.html

diagram_alt: Two tunnels on one device share its failure domain; a second site and device provide an independent path.

sources.supports: A second customer gateway and VPN connection can use the same virtual private gateway for redundancy.
Only one virtual private gateway can attach to a VPC at a time.

editorial_notes: Made second-site dependency reachability and independent uplink explicit.
